did_you_know.text: Did you know? Nehemiah served in the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes’s reign, and brought the king his wine even though he looked sad.
Did you know? Before answering the king’s request, Nehemiah prayed silently to the God of heaven.
Did you know? The king asked Nehemiah how long his journey would take and when he would return, and agreed to send him after Nehemiah specified the length of time.
Did you know? Nehemiah asked the king for a letter to Asaph, keeper of the royal park, so that he could obtain timber for the gates of the citadel, the city wall, and the house where he would live.
Did you know? Nehemiah arrived in the province Beyond the River with the king’s letters and accompanied by army officers and cavalry.
Did you know? After spending three days in Jerusalem, Nehemiah went out at night with a few men and did not tell them what God had put in his heart to do for the city.
Did you know? During his nighttime inspection, Nehemiah came to a passage so blocked that there was no room for the animal he was riding to pass through.
Did you know? After Nehemiah told the leaders about God’s help and the king’s words, they were encouraged and replied, “Let us rise up and build.”
Did you know? Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem mocked the Jews and claimed that rebuilding the wall was rebellion against the king.
Did you know? Nehemiah replied that the success of the building project depended on the God of heaven, and made it clear to his opponents that they had no share, right, or memorial in Jerusalem.
